# k0rdent_projects (Data Source)

Every project the token can reach.

The provider's `project` takes a project's `id`. This is where to find it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "k0rdent_projects" "all" {}

# The provider's `project` takes a project's id.
output "project_slugs" {
  value = data.k0rdent_projects.all.ids
}

# Only the active projects whose display name starts "ml-".
data "k0rdent_projects" "ml" {
  status             = "active"
  display_name_regex = "^ml-"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the projects whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `organization_id` (String) Only return projects in this organization. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `status` (String) Return only the projects whose `status` is this value. Sent to the platform as the list operation's own filter, and checked again on what comes back. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["active" "suspended" "disabled" "deleting"].

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the slugs, for `for_each` and `contains`. Same order as `projects`: sorted by `id`, then `organization_id`.
- `projects` (Attributes List) The projects. Sorted by `id`, then `organization_id`. That order is stable across reads but not across insertions, so a new project can shift every index after it: address them with `for_each` rather than `projects[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects))

<a id="nestedatt--projects"></a>
### Nested Schema for `projects`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read. Null when the project has none.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name. Null when the project has none.
- `id` (String) The id that goes in the provider's `project`.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization this project belongs to.
- `region` (String) The region the project is locked to, which every regional resource in it has to use. Null for a project made before regions were required.
- `self_link` (String) Server-defined URL for this project.
- `status` (String) `active`, `suspended`, `disabled` or `deleting`.
